properties.name: An idea in the graph stays connected to whether it was built and to where it was written — the user never hunts for the source document again
properties.statement:
Once an idea or requirement is in the design, reflow2 must keep it connected in BOTH directions without the user remembering it exists: FORWARD to the design and implementation that serve it (or the visible absence of any), and BACKWARD to the document and location it was written in. The user must never again have to recall that they wrote something, hunt for the file, and hand-point an agent at it.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-04, IN HIS OWN WORDS: "I put in dev_storyflow probably hundreds of ideas (some of which may be requirements) - I always struggled of translating these ideas into design and implementation. It was always manual process of me trying to find the document or documents that I had written the idea/requirement in and then purposefully point the agent to it. my hope is that by putting this in the graph, that these requirements are automatically linked to design and implementation (kind of a core feature of reflow2)."

WHAT "AUTOMATICALLY LINKED" MUST AND MUST NOT MEAN, because the obvious reading of his words would break the product. reflow2 must NOT auto-draw SATISFIES/REALIZES edges from similarity: the adopt skill's central discipline is that "a requirement backed out of the implementation that satisfies it is satisfied by construction — it can never contradict anything, so a graph of those can never say anything," and auto-linking would make every captured idea read as delivered and the completion reading say 100% forever. Edge PREDICTION is a live open question and deliberately framed as a question rather than a repair (dec:idea-missing-edge-prediction, proposed). What must be automatic is the INVERSE: an idea nothing implements FIRES AND KEEPS FIRING (unsatisfied_requirement — "a Requirement has no SATISFIES from any Capability", verified in detect.rs), and an idea that IS implemented is reachable to its file paths through the existing thread — Requirement <-SATISFIES- Capability -ALLOCATED_TO-> Component <-REALIZES- Artifact. The backward half is already carried by ingest: every extracted node gets YIELDED to its provenance Fragment, whose content_ref holds the blob hash plus the agent's locator (dec:agent-navigates-content).

⭐ THE RESTATEMENT THAT MATTERS, AND IT IS NOT THE PROBLEM AS FIRST DESCRIBED. The stated pain is retrieval — "I could not find the document." The operative pain is VISIBILITY: an idea written eighteen months ago was invisible until he happened to remember it existed. Auto-linking would restore that invisibility under a friendlier name, because a linked idea reads as handled. Staying LOUD until ruled on is therefore the requirement, and cheap retrieval is its by-product rather than its point.

DISTINCT FROM ITS TWO NEIGHBOURS, on the same pattern req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design uses to separate itself from req:corpus-ingest. req:corpus-ingest is CONVERGENCE (forty specs naming one component resolve to one node). req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design is INGEST (a contradictory, never-built corpus becomes a design at all). THIS one is what the design owes the user AFTERWARDS — it is satisfied or violated long after ingest has finished, and it is violated silently. req:golden-thread (accepted) states the thread must not break; this states that an idea's END of that thread must be loud when the thread does not reach it, which is the case a corpus makes normal rather than exceptional.

Status deliberately `proposed`: Anthony's framing captured in his words and awaiting his confirmation of the wording. The reading above ("loud, not linked") is MY restatement of what he asked for and is the part most worth his challenge — he asked for automatic linking and is being told the opposite is what serves him.
